name: cad_list_parts
description: List the designs in the CAD library (model rocket, quadcopter, gearbox, ...) with their descriptions and named presets, and which one is open on the desk.

name: cad_open_part
description: Open a design from the library on the desk and show it in the CAD view (opens the view if needed). `part` is an id from cad_list_parts (rocket, quadcopter, gearbox); a title or a word like 'drone' works too. Each design keeps its own history, so switching back resumes where it was.

name: cad_get_params
description: The open design: every parameter with its value, range and unit; its metrics, each with a status (ok, warn or bad; for the rocket, static margin in calibers: below 1.0 is unstable, 1.5 to 2.5 is good); its presets; its demo; and its part IDs.

name: cad_set_params
description: Change parameters of the open design; it regenerates in about a second, in the CAD view. Pass absolute values (work out '10% larger' from cad_get_params first). Match the user's words to the closest parameter (on the rocket the body tube is the 'shaft' or 'body'). Out-of-range values are clamped. Returns the new metrics: if one went bad, tell the user and suggest a fix.

request.description: What the user asked for, in a few of their words, e.g. "Make the fins smaller"; it names the version in the design's history.

name: cad_apply_preset
description: Apply one of the open design's named presets (from cad_get_params), on top of its current values. Returns the new metrics, like cad_set_params.

request.description: What the user asked for, in a few of their words (for the history; the preset's name if left out).

name: cad_undo
description: Undo the last change to the open design.

name: cad_reset
description: Put the open design back to its defaults (undo still works afterwards).

name: cad_view
description: Change how the open design is shown (view only; the design doesn't change). Pass only what the user asked for. expand: true brings the model up big in front of the user, where they can pull parts off and turn them ('expand it', 'let me look at it', 'bring it closer'); false puts it back on the desk. explode: true spreads the parts out, false puts them back together (also snaps pulled-off parts back). focus_id: highlight a part (IDs from cad_get_params, e.g. NOSE_CONE, FIN_1), several (FIN_1,FIN_3) or a group by prefix (FIN_* is every fin); empty string clears it. markers: the center of gravity and other markers on the model. dimensions: dimension callouts on the model. tab: the design panel's tab.

name: cad_take_part
description: Take one part off the open design and hand it to the user, or put it back ('hand me a fin', 'let me hold the nose cone', 'put it back'). This brings the model up big in front of the user too. part_id: a part ID from cad_get_params (FIN_1) or a group (FIN_* is any fin; asked again, Albie takes the next one). put_back: true puts it back; leave part_id out for the last part taken. To put every part back, use cad_view explode false.

name: cad_demo
description: Run the open design's demo in the CAD view: the rocket flies its simulated flight across the room, the quadcopter hovers, the gearbox turns at its ratio ('show me it flying', 'make it hover', 'run it'). run=false stops it. For the rocket it also returns the flight numbers (apogee in metres, speeds, landing): mention one. If the demo is blocked, say why.

name: cad_simulate_flight
description: Rocket designs only: the flight numbers on an Estes C6-5 without showing anything: apogee in metres, time to apogee, speeds, when the parachute opens, descent rate and landing time and distance (events). To show it flying, use cad_demo. If the result has a warning, mention it.

name: cad_list_versions
description: The open design's recent versions, oldest first: number, what made it (the request, preset or change), its main metric, and which one is current.

name: cad_restore_version
description: Go back to an earlier version (a number from cad_list_versions): its values become a new current version, so undo still works. Use cad_undo for just the last change.

name: cad_export_files
description: Make the open design's files for a supplier or a print shop: the CAD model (STEP), a mesh for 3D printing (STL), the engineering drawing (PDF) and the parts list (CSV). To send them to someone, use messages_send with attach instead; this only makes them and says what they are.

name: ml_open
description: Open a machine-learning project on the ML desk: the training, data and results panels unfold, with its last run. Without `project` it opens the one the user worked on last ('the ML stuff I've been working on'). Then say the last run's score from the result.

project.description: folder name or path, if the user named one (e.g. 'cifar10')

name: ml_github
description: Pull an ML project from GitHub and open it on the ML desk ('pull up the pytorch cifar repo'). First call it with what the user said: it finds the repo but downloads nothing. Say its name and owner and ask if that's the one. Only after a yes, call it again with confirm true and query set to the full_name it returned: it downloads the repo, works out what kind of model it is, and that model's panels unfold. A new repo takes about a minute; say you're setting it up. Any PyTorch or scikit-learn repo works, notebooks too; a folder URL (github.com/owner/repo/tree/main/mnist) opens just that example. Once it's ready, offer to train it (ml_train).

query.description: the repo as the user said it, owner/repo, or a GitHub URL (a /tree/<branch>/<folder> URL for one folder of it)

confirm.description: true only after the user said yes to the repo you found

name: ml_new
description: Start a NEW machine-learning project from scratch, for any request to make, build, start or train a new model or ML project ('start an RNN project', 'build a CNN on handwritten digits', 'train a transformer on movie reviews', 'fine-tune distilbert on movie reviews'). It picks a Hugging Face dataset, downloads a sample, writes the project's code (an RNN, LSTM, GRU, Transformer, CNN or MLP from scratch, or a pretrained Hugging Face encoder fine-tuned with a new head) and starts training: the ML desk opens by itself in about 10 to 30 seconds and the curves go live (a pretrained model's first run also downloads its weights, so it can take a couple of minutes). Pass what the user said; pass base_model when they named a Hugging Face model to fine-tune (e.g. 'distilbert', 'roberta-base', 'google/electra-small-discriminator'). Then say in one short sentence what you're building from the result (model, dataset, classes); the score is spoken when it finishes. Don't call ml_open or ml_train after it.

request.description: the user's own words for the project

model.description: the model the user named, if any ('hf' = fine-tune a pretrained encoder)

base_model.description: the Hugging Face model to fine-tune: an id (owner/name), a family ('distilbert', 'roberta'), or a model name the user said. Leave it out to train from scratch

dataset.description: a Hugging Face dataset id (owner/name) or what the data is about ('movie reviews', 'handwritten digits'), if the user said

task.description: only if the user was clear about text or images

epochs.description: how many epochs, if the user said (default 8 from scratch, 3 when fine-tuning)

publish.description: true if the user also asked to put it on GitHub or open a pull request; after training Albie asks before opening it

name: ml_publish
description: Put the ML project Albie built (ml_new) on GitHub as a pull request: its code, a README with the training results, and the data when it's small ('push it to GitHub', 'create a PR'). Call it first without confirm: nothing is posted, and you get the repo and branch; say them and ask 'open the pull request?'. Only after a clear yes, call it again with confirm true. If you already offered the pull request after training and the user said yes, call it with confirm true.

confirm.description: true only after the user said yes to this pull request

name: ml_status
description: The open ML project: whether it's training, and the last run's numbers (validation accuracy, train/val gap, weakest classes). Use it for 'how's my model doing?'.

name: ml_improve
description: The user asks how to make the model better ('what can I do better?', 'improve it'). Looks at the last run and writes a code change; it takes about half a minute and you will speak the suggestions yourself when they're ready, ending with whether to apply and retrain. Just say you're looking at the run. Nothing changes in their code until ml_apply.

name: ml_apply
description: Only after the user says yes to the suggested change: apply it to their code and start training again. The curves stream live; the new score is spoken when the run finishes.

name: ml_undo
description: Put the training code back the way it was before the applied improvement.

name: ml_train
description: Train the open ML project again (the Train button). The new score is spoken when it's done.

epochs.description: how many epochs, if the user said (default 10)

name: github_list_repos
description: The repos in the user's connected GitHub account, and which one is open in the code panel. These are the user's own code repos. To pull a public ML repo for training, use ml_github instead.

name: github_open_repo
description: Open one of the account's repos in the code panel ('open the truck repo', 'show me the code'). Returns its top folder so you can say what is in it.

repo.description: repo name or owner/name; leave out for the repo that is open in the code panel

name: github_open_file
description: Open a file from a repo in the code panel and get its text, so you can explain it. Read-only.

path.description: file path in the repo, e.g. src/controller.py

repo.description: repo name or owner/name; leave out for the repo that is open in the code panel

name: github_list_prs
description: Show a repo's open pull requests in the code panel and get the list.

repo.description: repo name or owner/name; leave out for the repo that is open in the code panel

name: github_show_pr
description: Show one pull request in the code panel (summary, changed files, diffs) and get its description and changes, so you can walk the user through it. Pass file to open one changed file's diff.

repo.description: repo name or owner/name; leave out for the repo that is open in the code panel

file.description: optional: a changed file to show the diff of

name: github_close_pr
description: Leave the pull requests and go back to the repo's files in the code panel.

name: github_approve_pr
description: Approve a pull request as the user's account. This is posted on GitHub for everyone to see. Call it first without confirm: nothing is posted, and you get the pull request to read back. Say its number and title and ask 'approve it?'. Only after a clear yes, call again with confirm true.

repo.description: repo name or owner/name; leave out for the repo that is open in the code panel

confirm.description: true only after the user said yes to exactly this pull request

name: github_merge_pr
description: Merge a pull request into its base branch. This changes the repo and can't be undone from here. Call it first without confirm: nothing is merged, and you get the pull request to read back. Say its number, title and the branch it goes into and ask 'merge it?'. Only after a clear yes, call again with confirm true.

repo.description: repo name or owner/name; leave out for the repo that is open in the code panel

confirm.description: true only after the user said yes to exactly this pull request

name: github_link_repo
description: Link a repo to the project that is open, so the code panel opens that repo whenever this project is open ('this repo is for the truck project').

repo.description: repo name or owner/name; leave out for the repo that is open in the code panel
